caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION:The chart illustrates negative log probabilities for clinically relevant tokens, comparing a baseline model (MistralV0.2-Base) to the same model fine-tuned on data from six clinical specialties. The x-axis represents the clinical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, presented in that order. The y-axis is labeled "Negative log probability" and spans from approximately -27 to -22, with tick labels at regular intervals of 1. For each specialty, there are two bars: one representing the baseline model (light blue) and one representing the fine-tuned model (varying shades of orange). The baseline model consistently has a higher (less negative) negative log probability than the fine-tuned models. The Gastro-tuned model (a shade of orange) generally exhibits the lowest negative log probability values across the specialties. The Infect group shows the largest difference in negative log probability between the baseline and fine-tuned models, with the baseline reaching approximately -23.5. The Cardio group shows the smallest difference, with a range of approximately 1.5 units. The bars are not sorted in any particular order beyond the order of the specialties listed on the x-axis, and no bars are visually emphasized.
